answer: Call each clone a ferrous. It must anchor on the trellis, where sponsor keys, endpoint proofs and vote history make twins collide. Power comes only from summit: non-transferable judged-work credit issued at a fixed rate each epoch and decaying unless re-earned. With N heads sharing that fixed issuance, per-head summit falls as 1/N while the influence threshold is convex, so 1,000 ferrous need distinct trellis slots and about N-squared elapsed epochs. It breaks if trellis merges aliases, summit is lent, or judges mint extra issuance.
